amendments.rule: **A verb the ASV renders as a light verb plus a complement heads on the complement, not on the light verb.** This is rule 31's test applied to a verb: drop each word in turn, and the head is the one whose loss loses the lexeme. `הַאֲזִין` → *Give ear unto* heads on *ear*, because *give* alone gives anything; so too `הִשְׁתַּחֲוָה` → *did obeisance*, `נוֹעַץ` → *took counsel*, `הִמְלִיךְ` → *make king*, `הוֹדָה` → *give thanks*, `כִּלָּה` → *made an end*, `עוּד` → *bear witness*, `חָנַן` → *make supplication*, `בּוֹשׁ` → *put to shame*. The complement need not be a noun: an adjective (`הִכְבִּיד` → *made heavy*, `גָּדַל` → *make greater*) and a second verb (`חָטָא` hiphil → *made to sin*, `אָכַל` → *did eat*) are read the same way. Rule 24's *lexical predicate over subjects and auxiliaries* is about `was gathered`, and must not be read as a preference for the English verb — that reasoning would head *make king* on *make*. **A phrasal particle is not a complement.** `שָׁלַח` → *put forth*, `סוּר` → *take away*, and `נָתַן` → *put away* are one lexical verb plus its particle, and the head stays on the verb; the same subtraction says so, since *forth* and *away* alone name nothing. **A supplied object is not a complement either, and that holds of any verb's rendering and not only a light verb's.** Where the ASV writes an object pronoun inside or beside a Hebrew verb's rendering — `וַיַּפֵּל` → *he let* ***it*** *fall*, `וַיַּשְׁקְ` → *gave* ***them*** *drink*, `אֲנִי שָׁמָעְתִּי` → *I have heard* ***it*** — read whether an object morpheme is present. Where one is, it takes the pronoun under rule 18 and the verb keeps the rest, as in `וַיַּעֲבִירֵם` → *caused* ***them*** *to pass through*. Where none is, the pronoun answers to no morpheme, is its own `added` unit under rule 30, and does not join the verb merely because it stands inside or beside its rendering; rule 17's permission reaches a pronoun realizing the verb's own person and number, which is a subject, and never an object the Hebrew does not write, exactly as that rule leaves a supplied lexical subject noun `added`. The verb's unit is discontinuous around such a pronoun under rule 25. **This applies only to a pronoun that truly supplies an object.** A reflexive pronoun the ASV uses to render the Hebrew verb's own voice or its elative sense is part of that verb's unit, because the source verb licenses it: `אִכַּף` → *bow myself* keeps *myself* with the Niphal verb and heads on *bow*, and `הִגְדִּיל עַל` → *magnified yourselves against* keeps *yourselves* with the Hiphil on the same ground. Position inside the English verb phrase is not what makes a word part of the verb's rendering — the complement, or the source verb's own voice or sense, must license it, and an unsupported object does not. **But a preposition the ASV supplies to reach the verb's own object is part of that rendering.** Where the Hebrew writes a bare direct object — no object marker on it and no preposition of its own — and the English verb reaches that object through a preposition the ASV has written, the preposition belongs to the verb's unit and not to the object noun's: `חָמְסוּ תוֹרָתִי` → *have done violence* ***to*** *my law*, `תְּבַצְּעִי רֵעַיִךְ` → *hast greedily gained* ***of*** *thy neighbors*, `הֵקַלּוּ אָב וָאֵם` → *have set light* ***by*** *father and mother*, `אֲבַקֵּשׁ אִישׁ` → *sought* ***for*** *a man*, `טָחוּ תָּפֵל` → *have daubed ... with untempered mortar*. This is rule 16's reasoning where no marker stands to take the word: the same subtraction test finds that dropping it diminishes nothing but the object relation, and the object noun's own English is the noun. The unit is discontinuous under rule 25 where other material stands between the verb and the preposition, and the head is unaffected — it stays on the lexical verb, or on the complement where this rule's light-verb clause puts it. Two limits. Where an object marker or a preposition of the object's own is present, that morpheme takes the word under rules 16 and 11, a present morpheme taking its English before a supplied reading does. And this does not touch rule 33: a function word supplied for an adverbial accusative is licensed by that noun's own case-function and stays with the noun, whereas a word supplied for a direct object is licensed by the English verb's valency, so read which the Hebrew noun is before placing it.
amendments.why: The rule's supplied-object clause was written inside the light-verb discussion and scoped by the words *inside such a rendering*, so it reached `וַיַּפֵּל` → *he let it fall* but not a plain transitive verb given a supplied object pronoun. EZK.35.13 `אֲנִי שָׁמָעְתִּי` → *I have heard it* is that case: no marker, no suffix and no object noun stands in the clause, and the *it* has to be `added` under rule 30 for exactly the reason the existing clause gives. Widening the clause to any verb's rendering, and saying plainly that rule 17's permission covers a subject pronoun and not an object, keeps a later pass from folding such a pronoun into the verb on the ground that the verb is not a light verb. The same verse supplies the counter-case that fixes the boundary, so the reflexive clause is extended to name the elative sense as well as the voice: MACULA tags תַּגְדִּילוּ Hiphil, not Hithpael, yet *yourselves* is still the verb's own rendering. Nothing else in the rule is changed, and no corpus row shown contradicts it.

conventions: אֲדֹנָי יְהוִה → *the Lord Jehovah* (35.3, 35.6, 35.11, 35.14). The noun אֲדֹנָי takes *the Lord*, its *the* being supplied with the noun under rule 29 since no article morpheme is present; MACULA's separately segmented 1cs suffix is `unrepresented`, the ASV writing nothing for it; and יְהוִה takes *Jehovah*. The four suffixes are BSB disagreements and are a documented convention difference, not errors.

After the oath formula חַי־אָנִי נְאֻם אֲדֹנָי יְהוִה, the particle that opens the apodosis is `unrepresented`: the asseverative כִּי of 35.6 and the waw of וְעָשִׂיתִי in 35.11. The ASV writes no connective at that clause's head, and the *therefore* it does write answers to the לָכֵן standing at the head of the verse (35.6 writes a second *therefore* for the waw of וְדָם יִרְדֲּפֶךָ, so the connectives and the morphemes count out even). Both particles are BSB disagreements and neither is an error.

Where a construct chain is rendered attributively under rule 28 and the ASV writes an indefinite article for the phrase — אֵיבַת עוֹלָם → *a perpetual enmity* (35.5), שִׁמְמוֹת עוֹלָם → *a perpetual desolation* (35.9) — the *a* joins the construct noun's unit under rule 15, which is therefore discontinuous around the attributive, and the nomen rectum takes only the attributive word (*perpetual*).

כְּשִׂמְחָתְךָ → *As thou didst rejoice* (35.15) is read as rule 52's preposition-plus-recast-clause with the parts divided as rule 18 divides an infinitive construct and its suffix: כְּ takes the subordinator *As*, the verbal noun שִׂמְחָה carries the lexeme with the supplied auxiliary (*didst rejoice*, headed on *rejoice*), and its suffix takes the subject pronoun *thou*. Rule 52 already licenses the preposition's half for a nominal object; the division of the noun and its suffix is recorded here rather than promoted, because the chapter has one instance of it and the corpus evidence before this pass did not reach the construction.

report: Read all 27 candidate lemma groups, then the whole dump end to end for the asymmetries the table cannot see (added units, function words folded into a neighbour). No construction is analysed two ways with nothing in the source to license the difference, so patches is empty.

הַר Ncmsc→Np is not a split: 35.3 and 35.15 write *O mount* because the ASV writes a vocative *O* there, and 35.2 and 35.7 do not. The same holds for לְ (a word where the ASV spends one — 35.12 *to*, 35.15 *unto* — and unrepresented under rule 40 where it writes a bare object or a double accusative: 35.7, 35.12, 35.14; the two identical אֶעֱשֶׂה־לָּךְ clauses of 35.14 and 35.15 differ only because the ASV writes *make thee desolate* in one and *do unto thee* in the other), for כְּ (*according to* 35.11, *When* 35.14, *As* 35.15), and for the waw connectives (*Moreover*, *Thus*, *therefore*, *whereas*, *and*), each read off the ASV under rule 14's open list.

The two הָיָה + possessive לְ clauses look like a split and are not. 35.5 הֱיוֹת לְךָ → *thou hast had* is rule 43 exactly: הָיָה takes the *have*, the לְ goes unrepresented, the suffix takes the subject pronoun. 35.10 לִי תִהְיֶינָה → *shall be mine* has no *have* in it; the ASV spends one English word on preposition plus suffix, so rule 30 fuses them and the written הָיָה keeps *shall be*.

Both `added` units are right and consistent with each other. 35.13 *it* is an object pronoun supplied for שָׁמָעְתִּי, which writes no marker, suffix or object noun; 35.15 *even* stands before כֻּלָּהּ, on which no object marker stands, which is rule 16's own limit. Neither is folded into a neighbour. The two reflexives that do stay with their verbs — *yourselves* on the Hiphil תַּגְדִּילוּ in 35.13 and *myself* on the Niphal נוֹדַעְתִּי in 35.11 — are licensed by the source verb's own voice, which is the distinction rule 44 draws, so the chapter is consistent on that pair too.

The 35.8 distributed בְּ (three *in*s on the one resumptive בָּהֶם, the suffix unrepresented) is the chapter's one genuinely contested edge. The verse note names the rule 33 alternative, which rule 8 requires and which is all a later reader can act on; the accepted reading follows the principle that a present morpheme takes its English before a supplied one does, and I left it. Note that the suffix is unrepresented under either reading, so the BSB flag on it is not evidence between them.

BSB: none of the 13 disagreements is an error. The six R tokens are the לְ of לֵאמֹר (35.1, 35.12, rule 27) and four prepositions the ASV's recasting silences (35.5, 35.7, 35.12, 35.14, rule 40); the four Sp1cs are the segmented suffix of אֲדֹנָי; the 35.6 כִּי and the 35.11 waw are the oath apodosis particle; the 35.8 Sp3mp is the resumptive suffix. Every one is BSB attaching a morpheme to its phrase where this project reads what the ASV actually writes. No edge changed to improve the rate.

Four conventions recorded, all judgments that recur across verses and none a restatement: the אֲדֹנָי יְהוִה formula, the unrepresented oath-apodosis particle, the indefinite article in an attributively rendered construct chain, and the 35.15 verbal noun recast as a finite clause. One amendment returned, to rule 44.
The chapter's textual decisions (WLC.EZK.35.9.v001 → r01, WLC.EZK.35.12.v002 → r00-base) are both compatible with the ASV as printed, so no rule 53 case arises anywhere in the chapter.
